draft.title: Samurai and bushido
card: warriors who fought for a lord. They were trained in the use of weapons such as the sword and the bow.
a lord who ruled an area of land. Samurai served a daimyo and were often paid in rice.
the code that samurai were expected to follow. Its main values were loyalty, honour and self-discipline.
Loyalty to a daimyo was meant to come before a samurai's own comfort or wishes. A samurai who broke the code was thought to have lost his honour.
draft.remember: Samurai fought for a daimyo and were guided by bushido, a code of loyalty, honour and self-discipline.

a.q: What was the main purpose of bushido for a samurai?
opts: It set out how a samurai should behave
It named the lands a samurai could own
It listed the weapons a samurai could use
It chose which daimyo a samurai would serve
a.why: Bushido was a code of values, so it guided behaviour through loyalty, honour and self-discipline. It was not a list of weapons or lands. Weapon training was part of being a samurai, but it was not what bushido set out.
a.clue: Think about what a code of values tells a person to do.

b.q: Kenji is a samurai. His daimyo is attacked, and Kenji stays to defend him even though he could escape. Which value of bushido does this best show?
b.why: Kenji puts his lord's safety before his own, which shows loyalty to his daimyo. Independence is tempting because he makes a hard choice, but bushido asked samurai to serve their lord, not to act for themselves.

a.best: It set out how a samurai should behave
